text: DSMC and kinetic transport DSMC approximates dilute-gas Boltzmann collisions by stochastic collisions between computational particles. It differs from deterministic pair-potential molecular dynamics and from self-consistent plasma PIC fields. Problem and representative equations Consider Boltzmann f with molecular velocity v, acceleration a and collision operator Q. A simulator particle represents F_N physical molecules. In a cell of volume V_c, sample pair collisions according to total cross section σ_T and relative speed g. Algorithm Move particles, apply wall/boundary interactions and sample collisions within cells. A representative no-time-counter algorithm uses a bound on gσ_T for candidate selection and acceptance. Specify hard-sphere, VHS or another collision model, distinguishing Bird’s early construction from later algorithms. Conditions and pitfalls DSMC uses dilute-gas and molecular-chaos assumptions. Compare cell size with mean free path and step size with mean collision time; adequate resolution is problem dependent. In low-speed flow, the macroscopic signal can be buried in thermal noise, and longer averaging does not remove discretization bias. The companion consists of homogeneous Maxwell-molecule elastic pair-collision rounds without positions. It is distinct from physical-time no-time-counter transport with cross sections/relative speeds, spatial hard-sphere motion, walls or inflow boundaries. What to check Test homogeneous velocity relaxation, Maxwellian equilibrium, wall-driven Couette flow or a rarefied shock. Check collision-level momentum/energy conservation, cell/step/particle-count sensitivity and uncertainty accounting for correlated samples. Derive moments on the finite-particle sphere with fixed momentum/energy here, comparing collision samples with independently projected and normalized Gaussian samples. Scalas et al. provide context for finite microcanonical distributions versus thermodynamic limits; this does not reproduce their complete hard-sphere calculation. Separate between-seed uncertainty and particle-count effects from momentum/energy conservation at each collision. For the finite system with fixed momentum/energy, a suitably normalized squared velocity component has a Beta distribution. Use this finite-particle reference for 16/64/256 particles and 64 seeds, separating finite-N bias relative to the Maxwell limit from sampling error. The distribution comparison follows 24 collision rounds; rounds are not converted into physical time. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Conservation and Maxwell relaxation in a homogeneous DSMC collision component Computation for a fixed target Test conservation and relaxation toward equilibrium through randomized pair collisions of homogeneous Maxwell molecules. This is an educational DSMC collision component. No spatial streaming, collision cells, speed-dependent hard-sphere selection, measured transport coefficients/flow fields or every-seed guarantee. Bird’s original hard-sphere conditions are not reproduced.
